text:
Root cause: `Files.Add` takes a raw `body io.Reader` and hands it straight to the request builder. Go's `http.NewRequestWithContext` only auto-populates `req.GetBody` (required for the retry transport to safely replay a request body) for three concrete types: `*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, `*strings.Reader`. A file opened with `os.Open`, or any multipart body streamed/wrapped around it, isn't one of those — so `GetBody` stays `nil` and `retryTransport` correctly (by design — see `TestRetryTransport_DoesNotRetryWhenBodyNotReplayable` in retry_test.go) refuses to retry it, since it can't safely re-send an unreplayable stream. That's not a bug in the retry transport itself — it's a footgun in `Files.Add`'s signature, which invites exactly this failure mode.

The codebase already has the fix pattern established elsewhere: `internal/multipartbody.NewFile` builds a multipart body into an in-memory buffer and hands back a `*bytes.Reader`, which *does* get an automatic `GetBody`. `CallLogsService.AddRecording` and `ProductsService.UploadImage` both use it already — `Files.Add` is the one place that never got the same treatment.

I'll add a `FilesService.Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts...)` convenience method mirroring `AddRecording`, keeping `Add` as-is for callers who need raw control.

## Summary

**Root cause of the retry failure:** `Files.Add` forwards a raw `io.Reader` straight into the request. `http.NewRequestWithContext` only auto-populates `req.GetBody` — which the SDK's retry transport requires to safely resend a request body — for three concrete types: `*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, `*strings.Reader`. A file from `os.Open`, or any multipart body streamed around it, is none of those, so `GetBody` stays `nil` and the retry transport correctly refuses to retry it (this is deliberate, covered by `TestRetryTransport_DoesNotRetryWhenBodyNotReplayable`), since replaying an unrewindable stream isn't safe. That's why every JSON-bodied call retries fine (those bodies are `bytes.Reader` after `json.Marshal`) while uploads silently don't.

**Fix:** added `FilesService.Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts...)` in `pipedrive/v1/files.go`, mirroring the pattern already used by `CallLogsService.AddRecording` and `ProductsService.UploadImage`. It uses the existing `internal/multipartbody.NewFile` helper to build the multipart body into an in-memory buffer and hand back a `*bytes.Reader` — which does get an automatic `GetBody`, so uploads now retry safely on 429/5xx like every other call. This also directly answers the ergonomics complaint: callers just pass a filename and a reader, no manual multipart construction. `Add` is unchanged (kept for callers needing raw control) but now documents the replayability requirement.

Added tests in `pipedrive/v1/files_test.go`: a basic `Upload` multipart round-trip test, an input-validation test, and `TestFilesService_Upload_RetriesOn429`, which drives a real client with `RetryPolicy{RetryAllMethods: true}` through a 429-then-200 handler and confirms the request is retried and succeeds. Full `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass.
